repo.description:
## Summary
An authenticated user with ordinary table write+read privileges can crash the entire `surreald` process (denial of service for all namespaces/databases/tenants on the instance) by accumulating a deeply-nested `val::Value` across many shallow requests and then triggering any of three recursion sinks that walk the value with no depth guard. Because `surrealdb-core` is built with `panic = 'abort'`, a stack overflow is an unconditional process abort. The deeply-nested value persists in storage, so it re-crashes on every subsequent read/SELECT and specifically crashes the admin `EXPORT`/backup - a persistent denial of service that survives restart until the poisoned record is purged out-of-band.

## Root Cause
Three post-parse code paths recurse over `val::Value` with NO cumulative depth counter:
- `convert_value_to_public_value` (`surrealdb/core/src/val/mod.rs:1169`) → `convert_array_to_public` (`:1256`) / `convert_object_to_public_map` (`:1274`) - mutual native recursion on the universal query-result path.
- `Value::fmt_sql` (`surrealdb/core/src/val/mod.rs:608`) → `Array::fmt_sql` (`surrealdb/core/src/val/array.rs:222`) - native recursion on the export/INFO path.
- `revision::to_vec` / `revision::from_slice` (`surrealdb/core/src/catalog/record.rs:71,88`) - the storage codec (revision 0.30.0) serializes/deserializes nested collections recursively with no depth guard.

The parser recursion caps (`object_recursion_limit=100`, `query_recursion_limit=20`, `expr_recursion_limit=128`, `syn/parser/mod.rs`) are per-parse; each read-modify-write request (`UPDATE deep:1 SET v=[v]`) adds only ONE structural level and stays far under them. The compute guard (`max_computation_depth=120` via `Options::dive`) bounds expression nesting, not the runtime nesting of a value being cloned/serialized. The only value-side depth guards (`val/object_extract`) bound idiom PATH length, not value nesting. The storage write path (`kvs/tx.rs`, `catalog/record.rs`) has no cumulative depth/size check.

## Impact
Denial of service (A:H) for the whole database engine process - all namespaces, databases and tenants on the instance. `panic='abort'` (`Cargo.toml:514`) makes any of the three overflows fatal. Requires only user-level table write+read (a scoped/record user with table write suffices). No non-default configuration required. Persistent aggravating factor: the deep value survives the write and re-crashes on every subsequent read and on admin EXPORT.

## Proof of Concept
```sql
CREATE deep:1 SET v = [];
-- repeat ~10^4+ times (separate RPC calls), each adds one level:
UPDATE deep:1 SET v = [v] RETURN NONE;
-- then any read overflows the stack and aborts the process:
SELECT v FROM deep:1;
```

## Attack Chain
1. Entry: authenticated user with table write+read → `CREATE deep:1 SET v = []`. Guard: none. Bypass: n/a.
2. Accumulate: loop `UPDATE deep:1 SET v = [v] RETURN NONE` (~10^4+ separate RPCs). Guard: per-parse caps (`object/query/expr_recursion_limit`) and compute cap (`max_computation_depth=120`). Bypass proof: each request adds exactly ONE structural level, never approaching a per-request cap; the store path (`catalog/record.rs:71`) encodes unconditionally with no cumulative depth check.
3. Sink: `SELECT v FROM deep:1` → `dbs/executor.rs:1648 convert_value_to_public_value` → `val/mod.rs:1256 convert_array_to_public` recurses to full stored depth. Guard: none. Bypass proof: direct source read on v3.2.0 confirms no depth counter in `convert_value_to_public_value` / `Value::fmt_sql` / `revision` (de)serialize.
4. Impact: native recursion overflows the ~8 MiB thread stack at depth in the tens-of-thousands → stack overflow → `panic='abort'` → whole `surreald` process aborts → DoS for all tenants. The persisted deep value re-crashes on every subsequent read/SELECT/admin-EXPORT.

## Bypass Evidence
- Parser/compute caps are per-request; each RMW step is shallow, so they never fire during accumulation.
- Store path has zero cumulative value-depth check (`kvs/tx.rs`, `catalog/record.rs:71`).
- All three post-parse sinks verified recursion-guard-free by direct read of `git show v3.2.0:<file>`.
- The four published recursion advisories (GHSA-6r8p-hpg7-825g, GHSA-q8qp-67f9-wr3f, GHSA-q729-696q-g9pq, GHSA-jv2j-mqmw-xvv5) all fix the PARSER (`Expr`/`Kind`/JSON parse trees) at parse time - none touches these `val::Value` serialization sinks. `expr_recursion_limit` (GHSA-jv2j fix) is present on v3.2.0 but rejects deep expressions at parse time; this finding's `val::Value` accumulation vector never re-enters the parser deep.

## Affected Versions
`<= 3.2.0` (verified present on the latest release tag v3.2.0 and on HEAD/nightly; no fix commit exists).

## Suggested Fix
Enforce a single value-nesting depth cap at the value boundaries - `convert_value_to_public_value` (`val/mod.rs:1169`), `Value::fmt_sql` (`val/mod.rs:608`), and `revision` (de)serialize (`catalog/record.rs:71,88`) - mirroring the parser caps and the flatbuffers `MAX_VERIFIER_DEPTH`.

---
Reported by **zx (Jace)** - GitHub: @manus-use
repo.summary: Unbounded recursion over persisted val::Value in response serializer, SQL formatter and storage codec causes process abort (DoS)
